newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MID WITS SHARES LEAPS ON UNBUNDLING NEWS.
newsitem.headline: MID WITS SHARES LEAPS ON UNBUNDLING NEWS.

text.p: Middle Witwatersrand (Western Areas) Ltd shares leapt on Thursday on news of an impending radical restructuring by parent company Anglovaal Ltd, dealers said.
"There is good demand for Mid Wits shares on the Anglovaal deal. People feel it will release strong growth potential for Mid Wits," a dealer said.

The shares reached a new year high of 21 rand, a gain of 200 cents or 10.53 percent, before settling at 125 cents higher, a gain of 125 cents or 6.58 percent. Shares traded were valued at over 6.9 million rand on a volume of 290,200 shares.

According to details of the restructuring released on Wednesday, Anglovaal Ltd will reorganise its gold holdings and strategic mineral and mining interests into two new companies, Avgold Ltd and Avmin Ltd.
Mid Wits will become the principal vehicle for holding the minerals and mining investments and will be renamed Avmin.
Another dealer said unbundlings usually unlocked value in shares and Mid Wits was a good buy.
"With a restructuring it comes alight that some shares are undervalued. So they become a good buy and it is money in the bank," he said.
Dealers said the share was coming off its earlier heights but would not trade below 20 rand.
"There is still some upward potential. I don't see them trading at below 20 rand. You will see the bulk of the trade at 20 rand or 20.50 rand," one dealer said.
